A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GPT4Scene and retain the same core framework and ScanAlign dataset. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot and fine-tuning experiments, component and resolution/frame ablations, and additional image/video benchmark results in the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark experiments and adds broader zero-shot comparisons, GPT-based answer judging, and robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: The specified 2D marker-placement rule changes from the projected mask's bounding-box center in v1 Section 4.1 to its centroid in v4 Section 3.1. This is a limited reported procedural revision; the architecture, BEV/STO framework, and training objective remain essentially unchanged.

E1.justification: The five ScanNet-derived 3D benchmarks and the appendix's image/video benchmarks are retained. v4 adds explicit small-object coverage and tests with missing markers and altered reconstruction conditions (Table 7), extending test scenarios within the existing indoor-scene domain.

E2.justification: v4's zero-shot comparison adds Gemini-1.5-Pro and Qwen2-VL-2B/72B. InternVL2 and MiniCPM remain in Table 2 but disappear from the full-metric appendix comparisons. The established task-specific and 3D-LLM comparator sets are otherwise largely retained.

E3.justification: v4 introduces GPT-4o judging of 1,000 ScanQA questions with weighted win/tie/loss scoring. New protocols also evaluate 1,000 small-object instances, 30% marker deletion, adaptive marker sizing, and SLAM3R reconstruction at three frame intervals. The original benchmark splits and base/HD/HDM configurations remain.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands robustness analysis through small-object, marker-degradation, and reconstruction-quality tests, and adds an isolated 'without STO markers' ablation (Tables 7–8). The separate BEV-only zero-shot condition from v1's pilot and five of its seven main qualitative examples are no longer shown; appendix examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new judging sample and win/tie/loss counts change evaluation design, not uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds zero-shot, judging, and robustness results and changes retained numerical entries. For example, 8-frame/256-resolution ScanRefer Acc@0.25 changes from 50.2 to 49.2. Main-table SQA3D HDM EM-1/EM-R1 changes from 59.4/62.4 to 60.6/63.3, while the appendix retains 59.4/62.4. Most captioning, grounding, and appendix image/video results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 Section 4.3 introduces a custom mathematical definition of GPT Score by aggregating wins, ties, and losses with weights 3, 1, and -1. Existing framework equations are predominantly notation refinements; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central framework, dataset, and fine-tuning contributions remain. v4 adds explicit robustness claims and extends the zero-shot applicability claim to large open-source models. Its conclusion also strengthens the zero-shot GPT-4o claim to state-of-the-art performance, although Table 2 still places it below Chat-Scene.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new robustness results as evidence that global-local correspondence matters more than precise reconstruction or marker accuracy. It also extends the model-capacity explanation using larger open-source models. These refine the existing mechanism and applicability discussion rather than replacing it.

D1.justification: v4 omits v1's batch size of 128, 1,283 training steps, 0.1 warmup ratio, and explicit Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct identifier. Learning rate, epoch count, hardware, approximate training time, and project URL remain. These omissions reduce documentation without establishing that the underlying training settings changed.

R1.justification: v4 adds recent spatial-VLM references, including Thinking in Space, Agent3D-Zero, and Video-3D LLM, alongside Gemini and SLAM3R. It revises discussion of complementary visual/point-cloud information and removes the explicit Set-of-Mark inspiration and citation. The principal vision-only positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, framework explanation, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The standalone Pilot Study section disappears, with its motivation incorporated into a reorganized experiments section separating zero-shot evaluation from fine-tuning. This substantially changes the narrative beyond merely adding experiments.

P2.justification: v4 removes the pilot bar chart, separates zero-shot results into a dedicated table, adds judging and three-panel robustness tables, and redesigns the seven-case qualitative figure around two cases. Existing tables are restructured and redistributed, while the appendix's qualitative figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The isolated-marker ablation and corruption/reconstruction tests address gaps in v1's validation of component reliability. However, v4 removes reproducibility details and introduces reporting problems: Table 6's GPT Scores of 465/1774 contradict the stated scoring rule, which yields -218/1462, and the stronger zero-shot SOTA claim conflicts with Table 2. SQA3D reporting also remains unreconciled across passages and tables. These empirical gains and losses in reporting reliability prevent a confident overall quality judgment.
